newsitem.title: USA: Ore. coalition proposes electricity restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Ore. coalition proposes electricity restructuring.

text.p: A coalition of Oregon industrial groups said Tuesday it has proposed legislation to restructure the state's electricity industry.
The bill would allow consumers to select their own electricity supplier by July 1, 1999, while including consumer protections such as minimum service standards.
Another coalition of consumer groups, the Fair and Clean Energy Coalition, has pushed for similar legislation.
The Oregon efforts come amid talk of federal legislation on electricity deregulation and the impact of existing deregulation at the wholesale level on Bonneville Power Administration (BPA).
BPA is the federal agency which markets power produced at federal hydropower projects in the Pacific Northwest.

"Oregon should develop its own plan now to shape our electricity marketplace before it is shaped for us by Congress or huge mega-utilities from other states," Julie Brandis, spokesperson for the Oregon Energy Coalition, said.
The coalition's legislation will be considered first by the House Power Deregulation Committee, which has received a series of briefings on electricity restructuring.
